references.text: God's original instruction to Moses to make carrying poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold for the table, which Bezalel is now executing.
A similar instruction regarding carrying poles of acacia wood overlaid with gold for the ark of the covenant, showing the same pattern for holy equipment.
Carrying poles of acacia wood overlaid with gold for the altar of incense, using the same construction method applied to the tabernacle's sacred objects.
Bezalel made carrying poles of acacia wood overlaid with gold for the ark, using the same material and technique as for the table's carrying poles.
Carrying poles of acacia wood overlaid with gold for the altar of burnt offering, demonstrating consistent use of materials in the tabernacle's construction.
Describes how the table was to be carried by the Levites during Israel's journey through the wilderness.
Contrasting material choices (bronze versus gold) that highlight the difference between the altar for sacrifice and the table for bread.
The divine instruction that was followed in the execution described in the source verse.
Parallel construction of the ark and the table, both designed to be carried during the journey.
Contrasting execution of the altar's carrying poles, emphasizing the difference in material symbolism.
The technical detail (the rings) that makes it possible to attach the poles described in the source verse.
